examples.en: There are many mountains in the northwest of this country.
It will snow in the northwestern region today.

examples.ko: 서북부 지역은 아침에 안개가 자주 껴요.
examples.en: The northwest area often has fog in the morning.
Our school is in the northwest part of the city.
Where do I take the bus going to the northwest?
Try finding the northwest part on the map.

explain: 어떤 지역의 서북쪽 부분을 말하고, '북서쪽'이라고도 해요. 날씨 예보나 지리 설명에서 지역 이름과 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My house is northwest of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서북부'와 같은 방향이지만 지역보다 방향을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same direction as 서북부, but used more for direction than for a region.

phrases.en: Tomorrow it will rain in the northwestern region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨 예보에서 가장 자주 듣는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The phrase you hear most in weather forecasts.

phrases.en: There are many parks in the northwest of this city.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에는'을 붙여 그 지역의 특징을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 에는 introduces a feature of that area.

explain_en: It refers to the northwest part of an area, and people also say '북서쪽'. It is often used with place names in weather forecasts and geography explanations.

t90.ax: Try finding the northwest part on the map.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 소각장이 우리 동네에 생긴다고 해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because they say a waste incineration plant is going to be built in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 소각장에서 나오는 열로 근처 아파트에 난방을 해요.
examples.en: They heat nearby apartments with the heat from the incineration plant.
The residents are opposing the construction of the incineration plant.

examples.ko: 소각장은 매연 때문에 늘 논란이 돼요.
examples.en: Incineration plants are always controversial because of the smoke.
A truck carrying waste to the incineration plant is passing by.

examples.ko: 공장 옆 소각장 때문에 냄새가 난다는 민원이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that the incineration plant next to the factory causes a smell.

explain: 쓰레기를 태워서 처리하는 곳이고, 땅에 묻어서 처리하는 곳은 '매립지'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '소각장 건설 반대'처럼 주민 갈등 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Residents gathered over the construction of the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 주민 갈등과 함께 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in news about resident disputes.

phrases.en: I'm worried about the air around the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소각장 가까이의 환경이나 생활을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the environment or life near the plant.

phrases.en: Sorted trash is burned at the incineration plant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰레기를 어디서 처리하는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain where trash gets disposed of.
phrases.en_equiv: to burn at the incineration plant

explain_en: This is a place that disposes of trash by burning it, while a place that buries trash is called '매립지'. In the news it often appears in stories about resident conflicts, such as opposition to building an incineration plant.

examples.ko: 서울 이남 지역은 오늘 날씨가 맑아요.
examples.en: The weather is clear in areas south of Seoul today.
I live south of the Han River.

examples.ko: 이 기차는 대전 이남으로는 가지 않아요.
examples.en: This train doesn't go south of Daejeon.

examples.ko: 이 강 이남은 새로 만든 도시예요.
examples.en: The area south of this river is a newly built city.

examples.ko: 충청도 이남에서는 비가 많이 내릴 거예요.
examples.en: It will rain a lot south of Chungcheong.

examples.ko: 이 도로 이남은 공사 때문에 길이 막혀요.
examples.en: The road south of here is jammed because of construction.

explain: 이남은 어떤 곳을 기준으로 그 남쪽 지역을 말해서 항상 '서울 이남', '한강 이남'처럼 앞에 기준 장소가 붙어요. 반대는 '이북'이에요. 그냥 '남쪽'이라고 하면 방향만 말하고 기준 장소가 없어도 돼요.

phrases.example: 대구 이남 지역에는 비가 많이 와요.
phrases.en: It rains a lot in the area south of Daegu.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이남'에 '지역'을 붙여서 기준 장소 아래쪽 전체 지역을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 지역 (area) to 이남 refers to the whole region south of a reference place.

phrases.en: I'm heading down to the area south of Daejeon this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기준 장소보다 남쪽으로 이동한다는 뜻이고, 이남 뒤에 '으로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means moving to the area south of a reference place; 으로 follows 이남.

phrases.en: It didn't snow south of Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이남과 비슷하지만 '남쪽'은 방향만 말해서 기준 장소가 없어도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 이남, but 남쪽 only gives a direction and doesn't need a reference place.

explain_en: 이남 means the region south of a reference point, so it always follows a place, as in '서울 이남' or '한강 이남'. Its opposite is '이북'. Plain '남쪽' just means the direction and needs no reference place.

examples.en: The old building was demolished.
All the signs beside the road were taken down.

examples.ko: 불법 건물은 다음 달에 철거될 예정이에요.
examples.en: The illegal building is set to be torn down next month.
A park will be built where it was demolished.

examples.ko: 낡은 아파트가 철거되는 동안 소음이 심했어요.
examples.en: The noise was bad while the old apartment was being demolished.
As the tents were removed, the square became spacious again.

explain: 철거되다는 건물, 시설, 간판처럼 세워져 있던 것이 치워져 없어질 때 써요. 철거 현장, 철거 공사 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 물건을 정리해서 버리는 '치우다'와 달리 구조물을 뜯어낸다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 철거된 건물 자리에 작은 공원이 생겼어요.
phrases.en: A small park appeared where the demolished building used to be.
phrases.nuance_ko: '철거되다'를 명사 앞에 붙여 이미 없어진 것을 말하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describing something that has already been removed.

phrases.example: 낡은 집이 헐려서 새 아파트가 들어와요.
phrases.en: The old house is being torn down and a new apartment building is coming in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '철거되다'와 비슷하지만 말할 때 쓰는 더 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 철거되다 but an easier, more spoken expression.

phrases.en: This bridge is scheduled to be demolished next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)ㄹ 예정이다'를 붙여 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -(으)ㄹ 예정이다, it describes a future plan.

explain_en: 철거되다 is used when something that stood, such as a building, facility or sign, is cleared away. It appears with words like 철거 현장 and 철거 공사. Unlike 치우다, which means tidying things away, it feels like tearing down a structure.

examples.en: The train slipped on the snowy track and derailed.
Service was delayed because a train derailed.

examples.ko: 아이가 탈선하지 않도록 부모가 관심을 가져 줘야 해요.
examples.en: Parents need to pay attention so their child doesn't go astray.

examples.ko: 그는 한때 나쁜 친구들과 어울리며 탈선했던 적이 있어요.
examples.en: He once went astray, hanging out with bad friends.

examples.ko: 이야기가 자꾸 탈선해서 원래 주제로 돌아가야겠어요.
examples.en: The conversation keeps going off track, so we should return to the original topic.

examples.ko: 청소년이 탈선하면 주변에서 먼저 따뜻하게 이야기를 들어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When a teenager goes astray, the people around should first listen warmly.

explain: 기차가 선로를 벗어난다는 뜻과, 사람이 바른 길에서 벗어나 엇나가거나 이야기가 옆길로 샌다는 비유로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 비유로는 '엇나가다', '삐뚤어지다', '옆길로 새다'도 많이 말해요. 사람에게 쓰면 꽤 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.en: A train derailment accident happened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차가 선로를 벗어난 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an accident where a train leaves the tracks.

phrases.en: The conversation keeps going off topic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기가 본래 주제에서 벗어날 때 일상에서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used in daily speech when talk drifts off the main topic.
phrases.en_equiv: to go off on a tangent

phrases.en: I went a little astray during my teenage years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 바른 길에서 벗어나는 비유에 쓰고, '탈선하다'보다 덜 무거워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people straying from the right path; less heavy than '탈선하다'.

explain_en: It means a train leaving the rails, and figuratively a person leaving the right path or a conversation going off on a tangent. In daily conversation, '엇나가다', '삐뚤어지다' and '옆길로 새다' are also common for the figurative sense. Used about a person, it is quite a heavy word.

examples.en: Applications for the event poured in all at once.
Orders flooded in, so packing got very delayed.
When visitors surge, the site slows down.
Calls with questions will flood in tomorrow.
I woke up to the sound of a motorcycle racing recklessly.
Requests are pouring in, so the server is shaky.

explain: '주문이 폭주하다', '접속이 폭주하다'처럼 한꺼번에 너무 많이 몰릴 때 써요. 또 차나 오토바이가 위험하게 마구 달릴 때도 써요. 주어는 주문, 신청, 문의 같은 말이 많아요.

phrases.en: Inquiries poured in when the new product came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주문' 말고도 문의, 신청처럼 한꺼번에 몰리는 것에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for inquiries and applications, not just orders.

phrases.example: 표를 팔기 시작하자 접속이 폭주해서 사이트가 멈췄어요.
phrases.en: Traffic surged when tickets went on sale, and the site froze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이트에 사람이 한꺼번에 몰릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people hit a website at once.

phrases.en: The reckless riders make noise every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오토바이를 위험하게 몰고 다니는 사람들을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for people who ride motorcycles recklessly.

explain_en: Used when too much arrives at once, as in '주문이 폭주하다' or '접속이 폭주하다'. It also describes a car or motorcycle racing dangerously. Typical subjects are 주문, 신청, and 문의.

examples.ko: 그가 돌연히 회의 중에 일어나서 나갔어요.
examples.en: He suddenly got up and left in the middle of the meeting.

examples.ko: 돌연히 비가 쏟아져서 모두 뛰어 들어갔어요.
examples.en: It suddenly poured, so everyone ran inside.
My friend abruptly cut off contact, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 방 안의 불이 돌연히 꺼져서 깜깜해졌어요.
examples.en: The lights in the room suddenly went out and it became pitch dark.
That player abruptly announced his retirement.
The child suddenly burst into tears, and I was flustered.

explain: '갑자기'와 뜻은 같지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '갑자기'를 쓰는 게 자연스럽고, '돌연'처럼 '히' 없이도 써요.

phrases.en: He suddenly said he would quit the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '히'를 빼도 같은 뜻이고 글에서 더 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning without '히', and more often seen in writing.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돌연히'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '돌연히' and much more natural in everyday conversation.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 돌연히 사라져서 팬들이 걱정했어요.
phrases.en: The singer suddenly disappeared, and fans were worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스처럼 딱딱한 느낌으로 갑작스러운 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a stiff, news-like tone for sudden events.

explain_en: It means the same as '갑자기' but sounds more formal, so it suits news and writing. In everyday conversation '갑자기' is more natural, and you can also say '돌연' without '히'.

t90.ax: It suddenly poured, so everyone ran inside.

examples.en: Accidents happen frequently on this road.
Power outages happen so often these days that it's inconvenient.

examples.ko: 우리 가게에는 외국인 손님이 빈번히 와요.
examples.en: Foreign customers come to our shop often.

examples.ko: 빈번히 연락하던 친구가 이사 간 뒤로 뜸해졌어요.
examples.en: A friend I used to contact often has become distant since moving away.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 빈번히 오류가 나서 쓰기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This app crashes so often that it's hard to use.

examples.ko: 비가 빈번히 내리는 계절에는 우산이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: In the season when it rains often, an umbrella is a must.

explain: '자주'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 더 딱딱해서 뉴스, 글, 설명에서 많이 나와요. 사고, 오류, 정전처럼 좋지 않은 일에 자주 붙고, 일상 대화에서는 '자주'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Earthquakes happen frequently these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빈번히'와 거의 같고, 동사 앞에서 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '빈번히' and easy to use before verbs.

phrases.example: 빈번한 사고 때문에 도로를 새로 고쳤어요.
phrases.en: The road was rebuilt because of the frequent accidents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '빈번하다'의 꾸미는 형태로, 안 좋은 일과 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '빈번하다', often paired with bad events.

phrases.en: I go to that cafe often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '빈번히'보다 '자주'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, '자주' is far more natural than '빈번히'.

explain_en: It means about the same as '자주' but sounds more formal, so it appears often in news, writing and explanations. It frequently goes with unwelcome things such as accidents, errors and outages. In casual talk, '자주' is more natural.

en: to be a long way off; to be remote

examples.en: Unification still seems a long way off.
Peace feels far away, but I do not give up.
It is still a long way off for our team to win the championship.

examples.ko: 해결이 요원할 줄 알았는데 생각보다 빨랐어요.
examples.en: I thought a solution was far off, but it came sooner than expected.
A dream that once seemed out of reach became reality.

examples.ko: 집을 사는 일은 지금 월급으로는 요원하죠.
examples.en: Buying a house is out of reach on my current salary.

explain: 시간이나 가능성이 아주 멀리 있어서 이루기 어려울 때 써요. '통일이 요원하다', '성공이 요원하다'처럼 목표나 희망에 붙여요. 거리가 먼 건 '멀다'를 써요. 주로 뉴스나 글에서 보여요.

phrases.en: That dream is still far off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요원하다'가 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 이루기 먼 일을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, pointing to something that is far from being achieved.

phrases.en: Success still looks far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하는 사람이 보기에 멀게 느껴진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that it looks far off from the speaker's view.

phrases.en: I still have a long way to go to the goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say the same thing.
phrases.en_equiv: still a long way to go

explain_en: Use it when something is so far away in time or likelihood that it is hard to achieve, as in '통일이 요원하다' or '성공이 요원하다'. Physical distance is '멀다'. It is a stiff word found in news and writing.

examples.en: This illness has an incubation period of about a week.
There are almost no symptoms during the incubation period.

examples.ko: 잠복기를 지난 뒤에 갑자기 열이 났어요.
examples.en: After the incubation period passed, I suddenly ran a fever.

examples.ko: 감염자가 잠복기에도 다른 사람에게 옮길 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can an infected person pass it on even during the incubation period?
How many days is the incubation period of the flu, usually?

examples.ko: 잠복기 동안 조심하라고 병원에서 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: The hospital told me to be careful during the incubation period.

explain: 병균이 몸에 들어온 뒤 증상이 나타나기 전까지의 기간이에요. '잠복기가 길다/짧다'처럼 말하고, 병원 안내나 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 증상이 시작된 뒤의 기간에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 이 병은 잠복기가 길어서 알아채기 어려워요.
phrases.en: This disease has a long incubation period, so it's hard to notice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증상이 나타나기까지 오래 걸린다는 뜻이에요. 반대는 '잠복기가 짧다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means symptoms take a long time to show; the opposite is '잠복기가 짧다'.

phrases.example: 바이러스는 잠복기를 거친 뒤에 증상이 나타나요.
phrases.en: Symptoms appear after the virus passes through the incubation period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증상이 나타나기 전 기간을 지난다는 뜻으로 설명하는 글에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means passing through the period before symptoms; common in explanatory texts.

phrases.example: 잠복기 동안에도 다른 사람에게 옮길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can pass it on to others even during the incubation period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증상이 없는 그 기간 안에 있다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Indicates being within the symptom-free period.

explain_en: It is the period after germs enter the body and before symptoms appear. You say things like '잠복기가 길다/짧다', and it is common in hospital notices and the news. It is not used for the time after symptoms have started.

examples.en: I'm worried about the economic slump dragging on.
As the war dragged on, prices went up.

examples.ko: 공사 장기화로 주민들이 불편을 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: Residents are suffering inconvenience because the construction is dragging on.
The situation is likely to drag on.

examples.ko: 파업 장기화에 따라 피해가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Damage is growing as the strike drags on.

examples.ko: 문제가 장기화되지 않도록 빨리 해결해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to solve the problem quickly so it doesn't drag on.

explain: 뉴스에서 '~이/가 장기화되다' 형태로 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '오래 끌다', '길어지다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: The construction has dragged on, which is inconvenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression common in news and writing.

phrases.en: The meeting ran long and ended late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '장기화되다' 대신 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural everyday substitute for '장기화되다'.

phrases.en: If you drag a problem out, it gets harder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 일부러든 어쩔 수 없이든 길게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is dragged out, on purpose or not.

explain_en: In the news it often appears as '~이/가 장기화되다'. In everyday conversation people usually say '오래 끌다' or '길어지다' instead.

examples.en: The road was blocked by a sudden downpour.
I was surprised when the company raised prices all of a sudden.
It was a surprise announcement, so there was no time to prepare.
It was so sudden that it was hard to respond.
Even when asked a surprise question, I answered calmly.
Citizens were startled by the policy announced out of the blue.

explain: 관형사로 분류되지만 실제로는 '기습적인', '기습적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요. '갑자기'와 달리 상대가 준비하지 못한 때에 하는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '기습적 인상', '기습적 폭우' 같은 말로 보여요.

phrases.en: Snow fell suddenly and unexpectedly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 꼴로, 예상 못 한 때에 갑자기라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a verb; means suddenly, when least expected.

phrases.en: Everyone was flustered by the sudden announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 준비 없이 갑자기 한 발표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to an announcement made without warning.

phrases.en: I couldn't answer the surprise question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상하지 못한 질문을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a question you did not expect.

explain_en: Although it is classified as a determiner, it is actually used with endings like '기습적인' and '기습적으로'. Unlike '갑자기', it implies doing something when the other side is unprepared. In the news you see phrases like '기습적 인상' (a surprise hike) and '기습적 폭우'.

t90.ax: The road was blocked by a sudden downpour.

en: to be mighty; to be powerful

examples.en: That team is really formidable.

examples.ko: 막강한 힘을 가진 회사가 시장을 이끌어요.
examples.en: A powerful company leads the market.
The opposing player was too strong.

examples.ko: 막강한 군대를 가진 나라는 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many countries have a mighty army.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 캐릭터가 막강해서 이기기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In this game the character is so strong that winning is easy.
His influence is known to be enormous.

explain: '강하다'보다 훨씬 세서 맞서기 어렵다는 느낌이에요. 힘·권력·팀·군대·영향력처럼 규모가 큰 대상에 어울려요. 작은 물건이 단단하다고 할 때는 '튼튼하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 막강한 군사력을 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: That country has mighty military power.
phrases.nuance_ko: '막강한' 뒤에 힘, 군사력, 권력 같은 큰 말이 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 막강한 is followed by big words like power, military strength, or authority.

phrases.en: Our team's attack was really powerful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 경기나 일에서 어느 쪽이 아주 셌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a side was very strong in a past game or event.

phrases.en: That company is not as mighty as it used to be.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 예전보다 힘이 약해졌다고 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form can say that something has become weaker than before.

explain_en: Much stronger than 강하다, with a sense that it is hard to stand against. It fits big things such as power, authority, teams, armies and influence. For a small sturdy object, use 튼튼하다 instead.

en: being unsuitable; being unfit; being inappropriate

examples.en: It was judged unsuitable in the inspection.
They say this water is not fit to drink.
The documents are unsuitable, so I have to submit them again.

examples.ko: 어린이에게 부적합한 내용이라 영화를 못 봤어요.
examples.en: The content was inappropriate for children, so I couldn't watch the movie.

examples.ko: 식품 안전 검사에서 부적합으로 나온 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: Products that fail the food safety inspection can't be sold.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제 성격에 부적합하다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think that job doesn't suit my personality.

explain: 반대말은 '적합'이고, 검사나 심사에서 '부적합 판정'처럼 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '안 맞아요'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '부적격'은 사람의 자격에 주로 쓰고, 부적합은 조건이나 기준에 안 맞을 때 써요.

phrases.en: This place is unsuitable for children to play in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합'을 형용사처럼 써서 어떤 일에 맞지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 부적합 like an adjective to say something does not suit a purpose.

phrases.example: 이 요리에 부적합한 재료를 쓰면 맛이 없어요.
phrases.en: If you use unsuitable ingredients for this dish, it won't taste good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부적합한 + 명사'로 기준에 맞지 않는 것을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 'unsuitable + noun' pattern for things that fail to meet a standard.

phrases.en: This job doesn't suit me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '부적합'을 쉽게 바꿔 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday way to say 부적합 in conversation.

explain_en: The opposite is '적합', and it often appears in inspections and reviews as '부적합 판정'. In everyday talk people usually say '안 맞아요'. '부적격' is mostly about a person's qualifications, while 부적합 is about not meeting conditions or standards.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 연결의 불안정성 때문에 자주 꺼져요.
examples.en: This app often shuts down because of its unstable connection.
The instability of the economy is growing.
Many young people worry about job insecurity.
They ran an inspection to check the bridge's instability.

examples.ko: 시장의 불안정성에 대비해서 돈을 모아 두고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving money to prepare for market instability.

examples.ko: 이 의자는 구조의 불안정성 때문에 쉽게 흔들려요.
examples.en: This chair wobbles easily because of its unstable structure.

explain: '불안정'에 '-성'이 붙어서, 그런 성질이 있다는 점을 짚어 말할 때 써요. 경제, 고용, 시스템, 구조처럼 설명하는 글에 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '불안정하다', '흔들리다'를 써요. 반의어는 '안정성'이에요.

phrases.en: The instability of the market is growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들리고 위험한 정도가 더 심해진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the degree of wobbliness and risk is getting worse.

phrases.en: We replaced the equipment to reduce the server's instability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 되는 흔들림을 적게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making the problematic instability smaller.

phrases.example: 고용의 불안정성 때문에 젊은 사람들이 걱정해요.
phrases.en: Young people are worried because of job insecurity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일자리가 안정되지 않은 문제를 설명하는 글에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in writing about the problem of unstable employment.

explain_en: With '-성' added to '불안정', it points out that something has this quality. It often appears in explanatory writing about the economy, employment, systems and structures, while daily speech uses '불안정하다' or '흔들리다'. The opposite is '안정성'.
